one_line_contribution: A provenance crossover that holds the optimized instruction and the test instances fixed and varies only which disjoint training half a retrieved-experience bank was distilled from (cells 6/7 and 9/10), so that the drop in memory's marginal gain can be split into an information-specific component the optimizer absorbed from the same episodes (Delta_info) and a generic headroom component that any better prompt would produce.
closest_prior_work: MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695) is the real threat, and the proposal concedes it. Its instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablations already measure how much of one training set's value each prompt container can carry, with the known finding that the split is task-dependent. A reviewer will ask whether Delta_info is more than rediscovering, with a retriever attached, that a demonstration container's marginal value falls once the instruction container has been optimized on the same data. The proposal's genuine increments over it are three: a query-conditioned read instead of static demos, distillation instead of raw exemplars, and the episode-provenance split (own vs other half) that MIPROv2 has no analogue of and that is what converts a confounded 'memory adds less' observation into an identified one. EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202, an ID I cannot independently verify) is the second threat: it reportedly places ReasoningBank, Memento and GEPA on the same 528/267 trajectories, which is the side-by-side table the earlier version of this proposal claimed did not exist. If its appendix contains any GEPA+retrieval cell, the combined-cell novelty collapses; the proposal asserts from a PI-supplied PDF that it does not. Experience Distillation (arXiv 2607.21051) already reports the same retention-ratio quantity with weights as the second container, so the ratio's shape is not new either -- only the choice of an optimized instruction as the rival container, and the crossover that makes it identifiable, are.
strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint is a difference between two already-small quantities, in exactly the regime the proposal's own evidence says is near zero, and the gating structure makes that worse rather than better. Delta_info is bounded above by the bank's total gain at the optimized instruction; the priors quoted in the proposal for this model class are +0.6pt (the program's own pilot, TOST-equivalent to zero for ExpeL on Qwen3.5-27B) to +3.6pt (ReasoningBank on Qwen3.5-27B). G1 then requires a >=4pt paired gain on S_dev with n=300 and SE=2.4pt, and A1 is chosen as the maximum over six agent-by-format pairings measured at that SE. That is selection on upward noise: the winner's dev estimate is inflated, its true S_test gain regresses toward the 1-3pt range, and Delta_info -- a fraction of that -- lands at roughly 1-2pt against the proposal's own stated MDE of 1.8-3.1pt. Risk factor 8 addresses only the inflation of S_raw by this selection; it does not address the deflation of power for Delta_info, which is the actual confirmatory test. The modal outcome is therefore outcome (i): a Delta_info CI covering zero, in an environment (BM25 multi-hop QA over HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki) that limitation 12 concedes is not where procedural memory is expected to be valuable. A paper reporting that memory and instruction cannot be distinguished where memory does nothing is not a finding about substitution. Compounding this: every claim a practitioner would quote is descriptive and underpowered. Prediction 4 ('I1_ab x M_ab <= max(I1_ab x M0, I0 x M_ab) + MDE', cells 12b-12d and 18b) is an accept-the-null equivalence run at 2 seeds with a ~4pt margin, and Prediction 7's compile-once claim is a TOST at +/-4pt -- a 4pt margin on a 4pt effect is not evidence of equivalence, it is a restatement of the noise floor. The paper's headline sentences would rest on its weakest arms while its best-powered arm answers a narrow mechanistic question.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Stop fixing the confirmatory environment in advance. Let the pre-registered screening choose the environment as well as the agent-by-bank pairing, or promote ALFWorld to primary -- E2 is described as the setting where task templates recur and 'procedural memory is maximally compilable', which is precisely where a substitution claim is worth making, and it is currently demoted to directional only because n=274 gives a 3.8-4.6pt floor. Buying that n (more task seeds, more decoding seeds, per-episode pairing) is a better use of compute than eighteen Tier-1 cells in an environment where the effect may not exist. (2) Gate on the contrast you actually test. G1 and G7 gate on acc(I0 x M_a) and on the unseen bank's gain, not on own-vs-other; add a dev-side estimate of the crossover contrast itself with its own floor, so the study proceeds only when the primary endpoint is measurable, not when a nuisance quantity is large. (3) Give the full-data question confirmatory status: 4 optimizer seeds on 12b-12d, and add the co-adapted full-data arm (see missing baseline), since Prediction 4 is the sentence readers will cite. (4) Cut ruthlessly. Cells 15, 18d, 20, 21, 23 and 25 are defensive; their compute belongs in seeds for cells 5-10 and 12b-12d. A 9-page paper with 25 arms, 16 predictions and five test families will be read as a program, not a result -- and if Delta_info is inconclusive, no amount of Tier-1 instrumentation rescues it.
missing_baseline: Two. Primary: I2_ab -- co-adaptation at full data. Cell 11 runs I2a (optimizer with the bank in context) only on half a, so the recommended deployment (cell 12d: I1_ab x C_ab, no retrieval) and Prediction 4 are both benchmarked against an instruction that never saw the bank at the data scale being recommended. The track this was proposed for is named for coupling a self-editing memory with a prompt optimizer; an area chair will ask why the coupled system is never run at full data, and 'the bank does not add to an optimized instruction' is not established until the optimizer that was allowed to see the bank on all 800 episodes has been beaten too. Secondary: a compute- or token-matched inference-time alternative. Injected memory is token-matched only against padded prompts (I3), against the compiled block (C_a), and against raw exemplars (R_a) -- i.e. only against other things in the prompt. It is never matched against spending the same budget on more search: e.g. I0 with the step limit raised from 8 to 10-11 calls, or best-of-2 sampling with the same total tokens. On BM25 multi-hop QA that baseline plausibly beats both containers, and if it does, the entire two-container framing is answering a question whose premise (that these are the relevant places to put the budget) has not been tested.
preprint_collision: This is a substantially better check than most I see, and it should be credited: it is dated (2026-09-03, prior scan 2026-08-21), it states its channels and query counts (15 HuggingFace queries, 244 papers, 54 by-id verifications), it names the closest paper and enumerates precisely what that paper does and does not contain, and -- unusually -- it explicitly withdraws v2's sentence that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other'. That is the behavior the field should reward. But the check's own verification channel is degraded in ways that undercut the conclusion it reaches. arXiv is unreachable from the node; abstracts were confirmed through web-search snippets; and the check itself documents that one such snippet misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 when the PDF says +3.6, and that v2 retracted five citations as unverifiable that all in fact exist. So the instrument has a demonstrated error rate in both directions, and the load-bearing novelty claim -- that EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) has no combined optimizer-plus-memory condition, no token matching and no paired statistics -- rests on a single PDF supplied by the PI and checked by the authors, with no independent channel. If a GEPA-plus-retrieval cell exists in any appendix of that paper or of a 2026 systems paper, the combined-cell contribution is gone, and the check acknowledges this as residual risk without closing it (the appendix of 2608.14036 is flagged as un-opened). One adjacent literature also appears unsearched: the check hunts for 'memory vs prompt optimization' collisions but not for the design primitive it actually turns on -- held-out-episode / data-provenance crossovers in the prompt-optimization and contamination literature, i.e. work asking whether an optimizer's gain is specific to the episodes it saw. That is where a scoop of the *method* (as opposed to the application) would live. Finally, a caveat about my own judgment here: every ID cited from 2602 through 2608 postdates what I can independently verify, so I can neither confirm nor refute EvoAgentBench, MemDelta, MemHarness, Experience Distillation or the skills papers. The novelty claim consequently rests entirely on the authors' scan, which makes the degraded verification channel a real weakness rather than a formality.
